text:
Lina (PM): Quick brain-dump: i'm sketching an "onramp launch canvas" for tenant-islands. need pragmatic launch gates that customers can sign up to. want to align infra/eng/sre/legal + sales asks here.
Noah (Eng): +1. i think the canvas should show explicit tradeoffs: latency SLO vs cost uplift, model compatibility, and allowed fallback behaviors.
Isha (Infra): Practically, we also need placement knobs: "hard affinity" (pinned region), "soft affinity" (preferred region, can overflow), and "no affinity". customers will pick per-tenant.
Carlos (SRE): From ops side: define canary ring rules. e.g., Pilot -> 1% traffic (20k tokens/day) for 48h, Canary -> 10% for 1 week, GA -> 100%. Automatic rollback if P95 or error budget triggers.
Maya (Solutions): Sales asked for a simple contract blurb: "we will make commercially reasonable efforts to keep latency within X and provide Y credits for outages > SLA." Legal wants clear definitions.
Legal (Legal): we'll need precise definitions of "outage" and "data residency fallback". also negotiation guidance for reserved capacity vs shared lanes. recommend two contract templates: pilot (no SLA) and reserved (SLA + credits).
Lina (PM): Good. Proposed launch gates on the canvas: Pilot entry (customer tech fit + runbook review), Canary (autoscale + telemetry validated), GA (SLA legal + billing integration).
Noah (Eng): Tech fit checklist: model compatibility matrix (model weight size, quantization supported), KV cache warmup < 10s for 99th percentile, batching tail latency within X ms.
Isha (Infra): Infra gating: autoscaler responds < 60s for 2x load, egress cost projection acceptable (< +30% monthly), placement constraints enforceable via scheduler.
Carlos (SRE): Observability gating: token-level cost per tenant, regional P95 heatmap, per-tenant error budget burn rate, incident playbook validated in tabletop.
Maya (Solutions): Customer acceptance criteria: (1) confirmed performance on their golden queries, (2) signed migration window, (3) clear rollback plan.
Lina (PM): Pricing question: do we offer pilot discounts or credit to offset early instability? Sales suggests a small credit so customers feel safe to test.
Legal (Legal): credits are fine but must be limited. also we should template a migration window clause: expected disruptions <= N mins per migration, with notice period.
Noah (Eng): Important runtime note: if we enable cross-region fallback, model variants must be stitchable. e.g., region A runs Q8 quantized variant, region B runs FP16. outputs must be semantically compatible or we need to flag version mismatches to callers.
Isha (Infra): That implies we need a model compatibility tag and traffic-stickiness TTL. plus a KV cache namespace separation for islands to avoid contamination.
Carlos (SRE): Recovery policy: on error budget breach: first route to local fallback model, if still failing then re-route to alternate region with SLA flagging. define per-tenant grace period (e.g., 10 mins) before marking impacted.
Maya (Solutions): For highly regulated customers sales wants an option: private deployment window (VPC/on-prem). that should be a separate lane with different gating (legal & infra heavy).
Lina (PM): Let's capture lanes on the canvas: Shared-hosted, Reserved-dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem). each lane gets its own acceptance criteria and billing terms.
Noah (Eng): For the pilot we should prefer Shared-hosted but with soft isolation (quota + burst reserve). Reserved lane requires capacity reservation and SLA.
Isha (Infra): Operationally: add placement policy: node labels for regulatory zones, egress tagging, and a placement enforcement webhook.
Carlos (SRE): Telemetry retention: keep pilot telemetry 30d, GA telemetry 90d. alerts: P95 increase > 20% or error rate > 0.5% over baseline triggers auto-rolloff.
Legal (Legal): also log data access controls and retention commitments, especially for private lane. include a short template for customers to sign regarding data export during region failover.
Lina (PM): Action items: - Isha: placement & egress policy design (2w spike) - Noah: compatibility matrix + KV cache TTL experiments (2w) - Carlos: draft runbooks + alert thresholds + canary playbook (1w) - Maya: sales one-pager + pilot contract blurb (1w) - Legal: draft pilot/paid-SLA contract templates (1w)
Noah (Eng): i'll prototype a replay harness to validate batching tails and quantized variant parity.
Isha (Infra): i'll produce egress cost delta for top 3 regions and a scheduler proposal.
Carlos (SRE): i'll mock a canary dashboard and incident flow with SLA compensation calc.
Maya (Solutions): i'll prep a one-pager explaining lanes, expected costs, and onboarding checklist for AE teams.
Legal (Legal): i'll drop two contract snippets into the shared drive and tag for review.
DeployBot: scheduled: platform-onramp-sync Wed 11:00. created task ONRAMP-321 in board.
Lina (PM): timeline idea: Pilot invites start in 6 weeks after spikes complete. Canary/GA depends on pilot results but target GA in next quarter.
Noah (Eng): technical unknowns logged: KV priming cost under heavy churn, cross-region serialization overhead, model glue-test semantics. will update with numbers.
Isha (Infra): also note risk: if many tenants select hard affinity it fragments capacity. need a guardrail: minimum commit size for reserved lane.
Maya (Solutions): can we offer a "migration concierge" for first 3 reserved customers to smooth the cutover? sales thinks that's valuable.
Legal (Legal): concierge is fine but needs defined scope/timeboxed playbook. i'll add liability limits.
Lina (PM): Ok let's keep momentum. please post short status updates in this thread next Tues. i'll consolidate the canvas and share with GTM. thanks everyone. :rocket:
